title: Count Greater Than X
directAnswer: Scan and increment a counter when `nums[i] > x`. O(n). (If sorted, binary search gives O(log n).)

remember.takeaway: Counting under a predicate is one guarded increment per element.
remember.formula: c=0; for v: if v>x: c++

problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums` and a value `x`, return how many elements are strictly greater than `x`.
understanding: One pass with a counter for elements exceeding x.

approaches.name: Count with predicate
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Count elements strictly greater than x: a **filtered count** — bump a counter whenever `nums[i] > x`.

**Why strict `>`.** 'Strictly greater' excludes elements equal to x; using `>=` would wrongly include them. Match the comparison to the wording.

**Why O(n) for unsorted.** With no order you must examine every element. But if the array were **sorted**, binary-searching the first index greater than x gives the count as `n − firstIndex` in O(log n) — the key optimisation to name.

This is the same predicate-count template as count-occurrences and sum-of-evens, with `> x` as the predicate.

code.python:
def count_greater(nums: list[int], x: int) -> int:
    return sum(1 for v in nums if v > x)

hints: Bump a counter on which condition?
Strict > excludes elements equal to x.
If the array were sorted, could you avoid scanning all of it?
approaches.insight: If the array were sorted, binary-searching the first element > x makes this O(log n).
approaches.complexityReasoning: one comparison per element for unsorted data; O(log n) via binary search if sorted.
